title: [VSC-20] VS Code: AgentSeatTracker port with seat wiring that passes the shared seat corpus
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-19 (task-b3daad343a474830a6bd243991d5353d), which lands moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json. This row must pass it UNCHANGED (held-out test).

Objective: a pure TypeScript port of JetBrains' AgentSeatTracker (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/AgentSeatTracker.kt): the same constructor callbacks (load, save, deregister) and operations (launched, closed, resendGone, acked), plus a dependency-injected wiring function so VSC-21 only has to plug real objects in: `wireAgentSeats({ tracker, onDidCloseTerminal, workerIdOf(terminal), onConnected, onAcked })` that calls closed() for a closed terminal it can map to a worker id, resendGone() on every connected transition, acked() on each ack, and returns a Disposable that unsubscribes all three.

Deliverable: new moe-vscode/src/util/AgentSeatTracker.ts (no vscode import and no runtime import: every dependency arrives as a parameter) and new moe-vscode/tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs that loads it under node:vm with a require map that throws on every name (tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loads the pure ManagedVm.ts this way), replays every corpus row, and tests wireAgentSeats with fake event sources.

Not in scope: AgentLauncher.ts, MoeDaemonClient.ts and extension.ts (VSC-21), any moe-jetbrains file, the corpus.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs replays every row of moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json against AgentSeatTracker.ts and passes, with failing ids reported together.

With fake event sources, wireAgentSeats calls closed() once for a closed terminal that maps to a worker id and not at all for one that does not, calls resendGone() on each connected transition, calls acked() for each ack, and after dispose() reacts to none of them.
AgentSeatTracker.ts loads under a require map that throws on every module name and contains no vscode reference.
A scratch-copy mutant in which acked() does not save makes the test fail (mutant discarded afterwards); client-seat-tracker.json and every moe-jetbrains file are unchanged by this task's diff.
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

implementationPlan.description:
Port the tracker and the wiring. Create moe-vscode/src/util/AgentSeatTracker.ts with the Write tool (rail: no shell writes to tracked files). It is a pure port of moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/AgentSeatTracker.kt: read that file and keep its doc comment's why, worded for terminals. The file has NO import, and never contains the text 'vscode' in any casing or 'require(' anywhere, comments included, because step 2's test greps the source. Export exactly:
- `interface SeatDisposable { dispose(): void }` and `type SeatEvent<T> = (listener: (value: T) => void) => SeatDisposable` (the editor's Event shape, so vscode.Event values plug straight in);
- `class AgentSeatTracker`, constructor `(load: () => readonly string[], private readonly save: (workerIds: string[]) => void, private readonly deregister: (workerId: string) => void)`, with TS-private fields named exactly `known: Set<string>` and `open: Set<string>` (no # fields: checkRef 2's mutant patches `this.known`), and methods launched/closed/resendGone/acked(workerId: string): void;
- `type SeatSink = Pick<AgentSeatTracker, 'closed' | 'resendGone' | 'acked'>`;
- `function wireAgentSeats<T>(seats: { tracker: SeatSink; onDidCloseTerminal: SeatEvent<T>; workerIdOf: (terminal: T) => string | undefined; onConnected: SeatEvent<string>; onAcked: SeatEvent<string> }): SeatDisposable`.
Tracker semantics. The corpus is the spec, and JS Set insertion order equals Kotlin LinkedHashSet order. launched: open.add(id); if the id is new to known, add it and save([...known]). closed: if open.delete(id), deregister(id). resendGone: first compute `[...known].filter(id => !open.has(id))`, then deregister each. This is Kotlin's filter-then-forEach, so a callback that re-enters the tracker cannot change the pass. acked: if known.delete(id), save([...known]). save always receives a fresh array.
Wiring: one `disposed` flag plus a subscriptions array.
- Close listener: return if disposed; id = workerIdOf(terminal); call tracker.closed(id) only for a non-empty id.
- Connection listener: call tracker.resendGone() only when the value === 'connected'. onConnected takes MoeDaemonClient.onConnectionChanged as-is, and that event also fires 'connecting' and 'disconnected'; say so in the function's doc comment.
- Ack listener: tracker.acked(id).
- dispose(): idempotent; it sets disposed first, then disposes every subscription once.
Error handling:
(a) VSC-21 feeds load() from untyped workspace JSON. The constructor keeps only the non-blank string entries of an array result (`typeof id === 'string' && id.trim() !== ''`, as Kotlin readAgentSeats filters isNotBlank), each first occurrence once. Any non-array value loads no seat: a stored string must not iterate as characters, and a number must not throw.
(b) If subscribing any source throws, dispose the subscriptions already made, then rethrow, so a half-wired tracker leaks no listener.
(c) Every listener returns early once disposed, so a late or leaky source reaches neither workerIdOf nor the tracker.
(d) Errors from load, save and deregister propagate unchanged, as in Kotlin, whose injected readAgentSeats and writeAgentSeats do their own catching; VSC-21's callbacks own that.
Add no other try/catch, no logger and no lock (the extension host is single-threaded). Keep the file eslint-clean (no any, no unused vars) and strict-tsc clean.
implementationPlan.note: Created AgentSeatTracker.ts via Write: pure port of the Kotlin tracker (TS-private known/open Sets, fresh array copies to save, resendGone computes the gone list before deregistering, load filtered to non-blank strings via storedIds with error handling for non-array values) plus wireAgentSeats (disposed flag, rollback on subscribe failure, 'connected'-only resend). Source grep: 0 matches for vscode/require(/import/non-ASCII. Shared checkout has 25 other dirty paths from other sessions; none touched.

implementationPlan.description:
Test the corpus replay, purity and wiring. Create moe-vscode/tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs with the Write tool. Use 'use strict', node:test and node:assert/strict. Load the source exactly as tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loads ManagedVm.ts: read the file text, run ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020), then vm.runInThisContext of the (exports, module, require) wrapper, passing a require that throws `AgentSeatTracker.ts must not require ${name}` for every name. Copy the harness (tests share no helper module). Name the source-text variable so it cannot clash with an event-source helper: the planning dry run hit a duplicate-identifier SyntaxError. Every test uses exact-value assertions:
P1 purity: the source matches none of /vscode/i, /^\s*import\b/m and /\brequire\s*\(/; AgentSeatTracker and wireAgentSeats are functions.
C1 corpus (mem:task-task-b3daad343a474830a6bd243991d5353d-handoff):
- Read path.join(__dirname, '../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json'). Assert version 1, at least 10 rows and unique ids.
- Replay each row as SeatTrackerCorpusTest.kt does. store = persisted. The tracker uses load () => store, save ids => { store = ids }, and a deregister that pushes to one log. launched, closed and acked call the tracker with workerId; connect calls resendGone(); restart builds a new tracker over the current store; the log spans restarts.
- Each of these is that row's failure, never a skip: an unknown op, a launched/closed/acked without a non-empty workerId, a connect/restart carrying a workerId key, a thrown error.
- Compare with util.isDeepStrictEqual, first against expectDeregistered, then expectPersisted, and record `${id}: expected deregistered|persisted <json>, got <json>`.
- End with ONE assert.deepEqual(failures, []), so every failing id is reported together.
L1 load: stored ['worker-aaaa1111', '', '  ', 7, null, {}, 'qa-bbbb2222', 'worker-aaaa1111'] makes resendGone() deregister exactly ['worker-aaaa1111', 'qa-bbbb2222'], and save is never called. undefined, null, 'worker-aaaa1111', 42 and { 0: 'worker-aaaa1111', length: 1 } each deregister [].
Wiring tests use three fixtures:
- fake sources that count subscriptions and disposals and really unsubscribe, plus a leaky variant whose dispose() keeps the listener and a variant that throws on subscribe;
- a recording tracker fake;
- two terminal objects: the seat maps to 'worker-aaaa1111' and a user shell maps to undefined.
W1: closing the shell records nothing; closing the seat records exactly [['closed', 'worker-aaaa1111']]; workerIdOf saw both objects.
W2: firing 'connecting', 'connected', 'disconnected', 'connecting', 'connected', undefined records exactly two resendGone calls.
W3: two acks record acked with each id, in order.
W4: call dispose() twice. Every source shows 1 subscription, 1 disposal and 0 listeners, and firing all three afterwards records nothing.
W5: with leaky sources, firing all three after dispose() reaches neither the tracker nor workerIdOf.
W6: onAcked throws on subscribe. wireAgentSeats rethrows that error, and the close and connection sources each show 1 disposal and 0 listeners.
W7: wire in a real AgentSeatTracker. launched(seat id), then close the seat, close the shell, fire 'connected', ack the seat id, fire 'connected'. The log ends as [seat id, seat id] and the saved list as [].
While iterating, run `cd moe-vscode && node --test tests/agent-seat-tracker.test.cjs`. Plain node resolves the TS6 typescript from WSL. Never run npm in the shared checkout.

It replays every row of the shared seat corpus (moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-seat-tracker.json) to the same deregistration log and saved list as the Kotlin tracker. The port also adds wireAgentSeats, which subscribes a tracker to three injected event sources (terminal close, connection state, deregistration ack) and returns one disposable that unsubscribes all three. wireAgentSeats calls closed(id) once per close of a terminal that workerIdOf maps to a non-empty id, and nothing for an unmapped terminal. It calls resendGone() once per 'connected' state and never for 'connecting', 'disconnected' or undefined, and acked(id) once per ack, in order.
After dispose(), which is idempotent, every subscription has been disposed exactly once, and no event reaches workerIdOf or the tracker, even from a source that keeps calling.
A subscription that throws while wiring disposes the subscriptions already made and rethrows.
The tracker loads only the non-blank string entries of an array, each first occurrence once; any other stored value loads no seat.

The snapshot gate (checkRef 1) exits 0 with 0 failed tests.
invariants: Only acked() removes a seat from the saved list. closed() deregisters only a seat that is open in this window, and only once. launched() saves only when the id is new.
save always receives a fresh array copy; the tracker never hands out its own Set.
AgentSeatTracker.ts has no import and no runtime dependency: every dependency is a parameter.
After dispose() the wiring never calls workerIdOf or the tracker again.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
onConnected:
- Typing it as a void event that fires only on connect was rejected. VSC-21 would have to adapt the client event, and passing client.onConnectionChanged where a `() => void` listener is expected compiles silently (a zero-argument listener is assignable), so it would resend on every state.
- Chosen: take the connection state and filter 'connected' inside the wiring, so VSC-21 plugs the client event in as-is.
Error catching:
- Catching load/save/deregister errors inside the tracker was rejected for Kotlin parity. JetBrains catches inside the injected readAgentSeats/writeAgentSeats, and VSC-21's callbacks own that.
- Load sanitation is kept, because it is a JS-only hazard: a stored string would iterate as characters.
- A per-seat try/catch in resendGone was rejected. Kotlin aborts too, and the seat is retried at the next connect.
Mutant:
- A test-only env var pointing the test at a mutant source was rejected.
- Instead, checkRef 2 copies the files and appends a prototype override, which is deterministic whatever the formatting.
planningNotes.risks:
Risks for this task:
- A #private field breaks checkRef 2's mutant. It then exits 1 and never passes falsely.
- The word 'vscode' in a comment fails P1.
- A `const source` text variable clashes with a `source()` event helper and gives a SyntaxError at load; the dry run hit this.
- Do not add a ts-only construct that transpileModule cannot handle alone (e.g. const enum across files); there is none here.
Notes for VSC-21 (not this task):
- Wire before the first client.connect(), or the startup resend of the previous session's seats waits for the next reconnect.
- load and save must catch, as Kotlin readAgentSeats and writeAgentSeats do.
- workspaceState.update returns a Thenable, so handle its rejection.
